svg.title: DDIA 8 · THE TROUBLE WITH DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS: sketchnote
svg.text: DDIA 8 · THE TROUBLE WITH DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS
On one machine, things either work or crash. Across machines you get partial failure: some parts work, some don't, and you often can't tell which.
From the client's side, all three look IDENTICAL: a timeout
The client only knows "no reply before the timeout". That is
why every retried operation must be idempotent.
Last-write-wins compares timestamps, and the causally later
write loses. No error is raised. NTP accuracy is only tens of
write file (thinks it holds the lock!)
Client 1 wakes up, checks nothing, and writes. Two writers
A late writer with an old token is rejected. The protection is
enforced by the resource, not trusted to the client.
"What if the payment provider times out?"
Outcome unknown. Retry with the same
idempotency key, or reconcile with a status query.
Fine for efficiency (avoid duplicate work). For
correctness add fencing tokens, or use the DB's
Wall clocks skew. Use a sequence from one leader,
a Kafka partition offset, or logical clocks (Ch 9).
"How do you detect a dead node?"
Heartbeats + timeouts tuned to p99.9, and accept
false positives. Leader election by majority, with
epochs to fence the old leader.
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.
